summary: Do not ship yet. R-1 is resolved by the exhaustive entry-point table, single-token migration, FIFO ordering, and corresponding tests (lines 205-227, 383-389). R-2 is resolved by explicit failure-isolation and lane-progress contracts plus reject-then-success coverage (lines 255-268, 390-393). R-3 remains open. No separate new critical/high issue was found in the fix.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md rules govern: render EVERY finding as a full table row, the human decides each row (accept/reject/defer/question — free text), echo back before applying, max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: R-3 still open: one retry does not establish a stable read
findings.body: The plan assumes one retry will naturally outlast eviction. A valid interleaving remains: pre-removal finishes, both reads occur while the writer is paused before manifest commit, and both therefore see the old manifest referencing removed chunks. The second read then falsely marks a healthy snapshot corrupt, violating story 38. S3's exhaustive scheduler should expose this, leaving an engineer unable to satisfy the stated acceptance criteria with the prescribed protocol.
findings.recommendation: Define an actual completion fence, such as waiting for a manifest-change/writer-completion signal with a bounded timeout before rereading, or route the read through the lane. Test retries that occur before commit, eventual commit, and writer termination after pre-removal.

next_steps: Replace the single-retry decision with a protocol that distinguishes an in-progress eviction from persistent corruption, then rerun the plan gate.
